extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, assignees, attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners handling statutory and terminal disclaimers
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and processing guidance for preparing, filing, and processing statutory and terminal disclaimers under 35 U.S.C. 253 and 37 CFR 1.321 (including special rules for double patenting, joint research agreements, eTerminal Disclaimers, signature/ownership requirements, and processing steps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory disclaimer scope and limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. 253(a) an owner may disclaim a complete claim or claims of a patent (statutory disclaimer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statutory disclaimer relinquishes legal rights to one or more complete claims of an issued patent but is not a vehicle for adding or amending claims; there is no provision in the statute or rules to add or amend claims via a statutory disclaimer. If patent is involved in interference or PTAB trial, see 37 CFR 41.127(a) and 42.80. A patent owner cannot avoid double patenting by disclaiming the earlier patent (Eli Lilly v. Barr).

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer definition and binding effect
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer disclaims or dedicates to the public the entire term, or any terminal part of the term, of a patent or patent to be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminal disclaimer is binding upon the grantee and its successors or assigns and must be recorded in the PTO. Filing a terminal disclaimer may affect patent term adjustment under 35 U.S.C. 154(b) (no adjustment beyond the expiration date specified). Sample acceptable language and forms (PTO/SB/25, PTO/AIA/25, etc.) are provided in the Chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required elements of a terminal disclaimer (37 CFR 1.321(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer recorded in the Office must: (1) be signed; (2) specify the portion of the term being disclaimed; (3) state the present extent of applicant’s or assignee's ownership interest in the patent to be granted; and (4) be accompanied by the fee set forth in § 1.20(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signature may be a copy (photocopy or facsimile) per 37 CFR 1.4(d)(1)(ii). The disclaimer should identify the disclaimant and their interest and specify the date when the disclaimer becomes effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements for disclaimers filed in a patent or reexamination proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: A statutory or terminal disclaimer filed in a patent or a reexamination proceeding must be signed by either (1) the patentee (assignee, inventor(s) as applicable), or (2) an attorney or agent of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A registered practitioner acting in a representative capacity under 37 CFR 1.34 is not permitted to sign the disclaimer. Where an attorney or agent of record signs, there is no need to comply with 37 CFR 3.73.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements for terminal disclaimers filed in an application (on/after Sept 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on or after September 16, 2012 a terminal disclaimer must be signed by the applicant or an attorney or agent of record (37 CFR 1.321(b)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this context 'applicant' refers to inventor(s) (including legal representative of deceased/incapacitated inventors) or the person applying under 37 CFR 1.43, 1.45, or 1.46 (which can include assignee or person showing proprietary interest).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements for terminal disclaimers filed in an application (pre-AIA / before Sept 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed before September 16, 2012, a terminal disclaimer must be signed by the proper party: (1) the applicant where application not assigned; (2) the applicant and assignee where each owns a part interest; (3) the assignee where assignee owns the entire interest; or (4) an attorney or agent of record (pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.321(b)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the assignee signs, compliance with pre-AIA 37 CFR 3.73(b) is required to establish assignee ownership unless an attorney or agent of record signs. To have an assignee who is not the applicant sign, the assignee must file a request to change the applicant under 37 CFR 1.46 and submit necessary statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entirety-of-ownership requirement to obviate nonstatutory double patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: To obviate a nonstatutory double patenting rejection, the entirety of the ownership must sign the terminal disclaimer disclaiming with respect to the reference on which the rejection is based (or multiple terminal disclaimers so disclaiming).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a 37 CFR 1.321(b)(1) applicant who is not the owner signs, or an applicant representing less than the entirety of ownership signs without others also filing disclaimers, the terminal disclaimer will not be entered and the NSDP rejection will not be withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer restrictions — no disclaimers of individual claims or conditional disclaimers
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer must be of a terminal portion of the term of the entire patent to be granted; a disclaimer of a terminal portion of the term of an individual claim or individual claims will not be accepted, and the statute does not provide for conditional disclaimers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclaimers contingent on PTA determinations, litigation outcomes, allowance of certain claims, or petitions are improper and cannot be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer timing and effectiveness (reference expiration)
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer filed under 37 CFR 1.321(c) or (d) after the expiration of the reference patent is not effective to obviate a nonstatutory double patenting rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts have held that filing a terminal disclaimer after expiration cannot undo unjustified timewise extension of exclusion (Boehringer Ingelheim v. Barr; In re Van Ornum).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required waiver/enforceability language for disclaimers based on joint research agreement (37 CFR 1.321(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer filed under 37 CFR 1.321(d) (to obviate NSDP based on a reference disqualified due to joint research agreement activities) must include a provision waiving the right to separately enforce any patent granted on that application (or patent under reexamination) and the reference patent, and must agree that any patent granted shall be enforceable only for and during such period that the patents are not separately enforced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is in addition to signature and other requirements; sample enforcement-waiver language is provided in the MPEP sample forms and form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of terminal disclaimers on patent term adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing a terminal disclaimer may affect any patent term adjustment under 35 U.S.C. 154(b); no patent the term of which has been disclaimed beyond a specified date may be adjusted beyond the expiration date specified in the disclaimer (35 U.S.C. 154(b)(2)(B)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consider PTA effects before filing a terminal disclaimer; see cases and MPEP references (e.g., In re Cellect, LLC).

rubrics_metrics.name: eTerminal Disclaimers (eTD) eligibility and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO provides eTerminal Disclaimers via the patent electronic filing system; an eTD may include up to 50 reference applications and 50 approved patents and is auto-processed if it meets all requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eTDs are accepted only for pending nonprovisional utility applications (including national stage and reissue) and pending design applications (including reissue). An eTD can only be used if: (1) the inventor(s) named as applicant(s) own 100%; (2) the assignee named as applicant owns 100%; or (3) a combination of inventor(s) and partial assignee(s) named as applicant(s) together own 100% of the entire right, title and interest. Requests for plant patent disclaimers or disclaimers based on joint research agreement must be filed by paper or scanned PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing responsibilities of Certificates of Correction Branch
rubrics_metrics.description: The Certificates of Correction Branch processes statutory disclaimers and terminal disclaimers (except terminal disclaimers filed in a pending application or reexamination proceeding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processing involves: (A) determining compliance with 35 U.S.C. 253 and 37 CFR 1.321(a) and 3.73; (B) notifying applicant/patentee when disclaimer is not acceptable; (C) recording disclaimers in the application file; (D) providing disclaimer data for printing in the Official Gazette; and (E) providing a certificate of correction for patents when a terminal disclaimer was entered during prosecution but the patent face was not amended to state the patent is subject to a terminal disclaimer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of paper or scanned terminal disclaimers in pending applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Paralegal Specialist in the Patent Legal Research Center processes terminal disclaimers filed other than eTDs for applications pending in a Technology Center (TC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paralegal will: (A) determine compliance with 35 U.S.C. 253 and 37 CFR 1.321 and 3.73 and fee application; (B) notify the examiner whether the terminal disclaimer is acceptable via a Terminal Disclaimer review decision form; and (C) where unacceptable, indicate nature of informalities so examiner can inform applicant in the next Office action. Paralegal approval is not an indication the terminal disclaimer correctly identifies the target application or patent — the examiner must verify the target before withdrawing any NSDP rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement terminal disclaimer when wrong reference identified
rubrics_metrics.description: If a terminal disclaimer identifies the wrong reference application or patent, a terminal disclaimer identifying the correct reference is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once a correct replacement terminal disclaimer is received, the next Office action should state the second terminal disclaimer replaces the first and the first is void. A second terminal disclaimer fee should not be charged because the first fee is applied to the second terminal disclaimer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple copending applications and terminal disclaimer coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: When two or more copending applications share overlapping inventive entities or ownership and would raise double patenting issues, provisional NSDP rejections should be made and maintained until obviated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If three applications contain conflicting claims such that provisional NSDP rejections exist in each based on the other two, it is not sufficient to file a terminal disclaimer in only one application; an appropriate terminal disclaimer must be filed in at least two of the applications (and sometimes in all three) to require common ownership or enforcement for all applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carrying over of terminal disclaimers to continuing proceedings and reexaminations/reissues
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer filed in a parent application normally has no effect on a continuing application claiming benefit of the parent, except it carries over to a Continued Prosecution Application (CPA) that retains the same application number; terminal disclaimers filed during prosecution continue to operate in reexamination and reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant does not want a terminal disclaimer to carry over to a CPA, a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 with required fee may be filed requesting the disclaimer not be carried over. Filing an RCE does not create a new application and the terminal disclaimer continues to operate. For reissue applications, a copy of an originally filed and approved terminal disclaimer need not be filed; the disclaimer will be effective for the reissue patent even if the front page of the reissue patent does not indicate it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of correction requirement when terminal disclaimer filed after issue fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Any terminal disclaimer submitted after the date of payment of the issue fee but prior to patent grant date must include a certificate of correction requesting that the face of the patent be amended to state that the patent is subject to a terminal disclaimer, unless the face already includes such language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures the patent front page and issue notices properly reflect the patent's status with respect to a terminal disclaimer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sample form language and permissibility of exculpatory language
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may use provided sample terminal disclaimer form paragraphs and forms (PTO/SB/25, PTO/AIA/25, PTO/SB/26, etc.) as examples of acceptable language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exculpatory language such as 'In making the above disclaimer, the owner does not disclaim...' is permissible in a terminal disclaimer; forms and paragraph examples are provided at the end of the MPEP chapter for Office action attachment.
